references.text: God reminds Israel that he brought them out of Egypt on eagles' wings, the same act of salvation mentioned in 20:2
Parallel to the Ten Commandments in Deuteronomy, where God identifies himself as the one who brought Israel out of Egypt
Reminder that the Lord brought Israel out of the house of slavery in Egypt
God declares that he is the Lord who brought them out of Egypt, the basis for keeping his commandments
God identifies himself as the Lord who brought Israel out of Egypt to give them the land of Canaan
God declares that he is the Lord their God who brought them out of Egypt
The psalm quotes God's self-presentation as the one who brought Israel up from Egypt
The Lord declares that he has been Israel's God since they were in Egypt
God reminds that he is the Lord their God from Egypt, and that they shall know no other god
Stephen refers to Moses who led the people out of Egypt with signs and wonders
Hebrews quotes Jeremiah and refers to when God took Israel's fathers by the hand and brought them out of Egypt
Confirms that deliverance from Egypt is the theological precondition for God's relationship with his people.
Specifies the meaning of deliverance by describing God's action as breaking the yoke of oppression.
Links the Exodus event directly to the call for a holy life in response to God's liberating grace.
Shows the goal of the Exodus: that God may dwell among his people as their God.
Shows the connection between God's promise of deliverance (chapter 6) and the fulfillment of this promise (chapter 20).
